title: Missipaug (Big Fresh Pond)
summary: Missipaug is listed as a name suggested for Big Fresh Pond near North Sea. The name points to a real Southampton pond while also showing how some Native-sounding Long Island names were created or regularized by later writers.
address_label: Big Fresh Pond, North Sea, Southampton, NY
history_content: Missipaug is a documented printed suggestion rather than a deeply attested early place name. The name preserves the distinction between the modern pond and the later name applied to it.
translation_content:
The form is explained as meaning "great water place" or "big fresh pond," built from missi, "great," and -paug, "water-place" or "pond." No alternate spellings are listed in the source entry.

Why Place Names Matter

“Geographical names are of great historical and contemporary significance for Indigenous Nations. They are strong expressions of cultural identity, and their conservation and continued use promotes the vitality of Indigenous languages and cultural knowledge.”

— Geographical Names Board of Canada, Best Practices for Indigenous Place Naming (2025), Context, section 2.2
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for modern Big Fresh Pond in North Sea, Town of Southampton. It does not claim to identify an exact historic Indigenous boundary or named place.
